key_insight: CLINLENS is a new benchmark for evaluating coding agents on longitudinal, multimodal clinical data science across linked patient records.
clinical_relevance: It targets realistic clinical analysis workflows that combine charts, notes, ECGs, imaging, and echo data, making it more representative than isolated QA tasks.
method: Built 200 executable tasks over five linked MIMIC data resources.
Used a 4 x 5 taxonomy spanning patient-time scopes and analysis capabilities.
Paired each task with private reference workflows and checks for artifacts, cohort/temporal logic, and final answers.
evidence_signal: On a fixed 126-task suite, the best of 24 model-scaffold setups reached 56.3% scope-macro STRICTPASS despite 100% execution success, while adapted biomedical systems peaked at 2.9%.
watch_item: High execution success can still hide incorrect clinical reasoning, so runnable code should not be taken as evidence of correct analysis.
paper_title: ClinLens: Towards Long-Horizon Coding Agents for Longitudinal Multimodal Clinical Data Science
